q1.explanationZh: 男孩说他们终于到达海边时（got to the coast）觉得太棒了，在那里玩得很开心。C 错：去的路上只是经过一个大城市；A 错：回来时只是从山附近经过，并没有停下来。

q2.explanationZh: 男孩说下午的体育课需要足球装备（football kit）。C 错：他本来想带笔记本电脑，但妈妈建议他用图书馆的电脑，他同意了；A 错：小提琴课是明天。

q3.explanationZh: 男孩建议换个活动去滑冰（ice skating），女孩说就听你的（I'll go for your suggestion）。C 错：这周没有好电影，电影院下次再去；A 错：游泳池是表亲们上次来时去的地方。

q4.explanationZh: 售票处就在妈妈上班的地方旁边，她用午休时间排队买到了票（in the queue）。B 错：网站出了问题，网上没买成；A 错：手机应用上的票更贵，所以没用。

q5.explanationZh: 男孩说：“你提议骑马上山真是个好主意，骑马（on horse-back）比我上次骑山地车容易多了。”B 错：他以前骑山地车只到了半山腰；C 错：女孩只是说常看到别人徒步上山。

q6.explanationZh: 老师最后说：“请大家回到笔记本电脑前，我们开始学习要用的软件。”B 错：食物链海报已经做好了，要放到学校大厅展出；C 错：Food Week 只是学校这周的活动，今天课上要学软件。

q7.explanationZh: 女孩想起来她把球拍和网球服一起放在了床上（on my bed），也就是在她的卧室里。C 错：爸爸以为在门边，但并不在那里；A 错：放在客厅的是网球包，不是球拍。

q8.explanationZh: 女孩问会不会画静物，又说“不知道那会包括什么，我得去了解一下”，说明她对课上要学什么很好奇。B 错：她说没怎么学过美术也没关系，并不担心；C 错：她没有说希望提高创作能力。

q9.explanationZh: 女孩说就是排队太长，男孩马上同意（Tell me about it），说要是不用站着等那么久就好了——两人都希望出餐快一些。A 错：女孩说饭菜不算贵；B 错：女孩认为每天都能找到不同的饭菜。

q10.explanationZh: 女孩说“你连想都不该想”，这种节目只会让参赛的人出丑，还说会有很多认真的对手——她在劝男孩不要参加。A 错：她没有提到比赛规则；C 错：她没有教男孩怎样获胜。

q11.explanationZh: 男孩说网上资料很多，他发现的每样东西都让他想知道更多（makes me want to know more），说明他觉得做研究很有意思。B 错：女孩问是不是很难找资料，他说正好相反；A 错：他说机器人技术是重要的话题，大多数人都有自己的看法，并不冷门。

q12.explanationZh: 女孩说电视上总是足球和橄榄球，如果有别的节目就好了（other things on too），即体育节目种类不够多。B 错：她说不介意专家们讨论比赛，觉得还挺有趣；C 错：她说自己可以反复看体操片段，不是在抱怨重复。

q13.explanationZh: 女孩在讲自己周末参加的野外采食活动：辨认野生香草和果子，找到了野蒜叶和接骨木花——她在描述自己做过的事。A 错：她猜到男孩会觉得无聊，并没有劝他去；C 错：她只说接骨木花可以做冷饮，没说自己要做什么。

q14.explanationZh: 老师说大巴八点半出发（It’ll leave at half past eight）。8:15 是到学校集合的最晚时间，9 点是博物馆开门的时间。

q15.explanationZh: 老师说路上需要带些水，但不能带别的饮料（You’ll need some water），而且车上不允许吃东西。

q16.explanationZh: 博物馆会给每人一支笔，可以留作这一天的纪念（a nice souvenir）。问卷做完要交给老师检查，不能留下。

q17.explanationZh: 老师说最新的展览讲的是过去城里怎样做巧克力，每个去过的人都在谈论它，所以很出名。做面包只是老街展里可能看到的情景。

q18.explanationZh: 博物馆商店有很多好书，还有各种各样的海报（a great range of posters）。食物要到附近的小吃店买。

q19.explanationZh: 网址是 www.waysbury.com，录音中逐个字母拼出 W-A-Y-S-B-U-R-Y，注意拼写。

q20.explanationZh: Mary 每天回家路上都会经过高年级学生的课后滑板活动，她觉得看起来很不错（I liked the look of it），于是喜欢上了滑板。A 错：她想劝哥哥们一起学，但他们不感兴趣；C 错：电视节目是她后来才看的。

q21.explanationZh: Mary 说开始玩滑板后，觉得鼓励其他女孩一起参与是个好主意，也就是想和她们分享自己的爱好。B 错：别人以为她不喜欢做滑板公园里唯一的女孩，其实她不介意，而且她们有时还和男孩一起滑；C 错：她没有提到想交新朋友。

q22.explanationZh: 有些人对她说“为什么不选一项不那么危险的运动”，让她很烦，她认为这些人不知道事故其实很少——他们觉得滑板不安全。B 错：镇议会同意资助俱乐部，没有人反对花钱；C 错：没有人说滑板不是好的锻炼。

q23.explanationZh: Mary 说让她惊讶的是俱乐部成员彼此相处得这么好（like each other so much）。A 错：成员水平各不相同，这在她意料之中；B 错：大家尊重她，她觉得可以理解，并不惊讶。

q24.explanationZh: Judy Blake 向她们提了很多提高水平的建议，还推荐了有好视频的网站（suggesting loads of things we could do to improve our performances）。A 错：一开始害羞的是俱乐部的成员，不是 Judy；C 错：她只是推荐了视频网站，没有要拍摄她们。

q25.explanationZh: Mary 说滑板已经成为奥运项目，她最大的梦想就是参加奥运会（my greatest ambition is to take part）——也就是参加国际比赛。B 错：大公司生产装备只是她提到的影响；C 错：她说当滑板教练不是她现在考虑的事。

content.v: Test Two. There are four parts to the test. You will hear each part twice. We will now stop for a moment. Please ask any questions now because you must not speak during the test.
Now open your question papers and look at Part One.
For each question, choose the correct answer. Look at question one.
One. Where did the boy spend his holiday?
Hey, how was your holiday?
It was great, thanks.
Did you go by car?

Yes, the journey took ages and my sister and I got a bit bored. We passed through a big city on our way. But when we finally got to the coast it was awesome and we had great fun there. On the way back we took a different route and went really close to some mountains, but we didn’t stop – Dad was driving! I’d really like to go back there one day!
Two. What does the boy have to take to school today?
My school bag’s so heavy today, Mum!
Well, can’t you leave something at home?
Not really, I’ll need my football kit for my sports class this afternoon and I really need my laptop, because I have to prepare a presentation for history.
Could you do that on a computer in the library?
Yeah, I’m sure I’ll have time to go there after sports class. That’s a good idea, Mum.
Well, at least your violin lesson isn’t until tomorrow, or you’d really have a lot to carry!
Three. Where will the girl go at the weekend?
Hi Sally. What’s wrong? You look worried!
My cousins are coming at the weekend and I’m trying to think of a fun activity to do with them. I wondered about seeing a film.
I don’t think there’s anything good on this week.
Well then maybe we’d better do something active. They all enjoyed going to the pool last time they came.
I know everyone loves swimming, but what about ice skating for a change?
You know, I think I’ll go for your suggestion! We can always go to the cinema next time.
Four. How did the girl’s mother get tickets for the concert?
Did you get tickets for the concert?

Mum got them actually. We looked online as soon as they went on sale but there were problems with the website and we kept losing the internet connection. It was so annoying! The ticket office is right next to where she works. We knew there’d be loads of people trying to get them, though. I suggested getting them from a ticket-sales app on the phone, but they were more expensive there, so she spent her lunch break in the queue getting them!
Wow! Your mum’s awesome!
Five. How did they get to the top of the mountain?
That was quite a climb! It was worth it, though – just look at that view! I’ve always watched people hiking up this mountain from back in the village. I’ve never actually reached the top before now.

Great idea of yours to ride up – it was a lot easier on horse-back than when I tried to come up on my mountain bike. I only got to about halfway and then I had to turn around – my legs were really hurting. It was fun racing back down, though!
Six. What will the students do in today’s biology class?

Right, everyone. I hope you’re enjoying Food Week here at school. You’ve all worked so hard on your posters of the food chain that I thought, rather than display them in the classroom, we’d put them in the school hall for everyone else to take a look at. It’s been great practice for the presentations you’re going to do in a few days. If you can all go back to the laptops, we’ll start learning about the software you’ll need to use.
Seven. Where has the girl left her tennis racket?
Dad – can you help me?
What is it?
I can’t find my tennis racket and we’ve got to leave for my lesson soon.
I’m sure I saw it by the door last night. Next to your tennis bag?
No, it’s not there, and my tennis bag’s in the living room.
Maybe you took it to your bedroom?
I remember now – I put it on my bed with my tennis clothes ready to take! I’ll just get my bag and put everything in it. Then we can go.
That is the end of Part One.
Now look at Part Two. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Eight. You will hear two friends talking about going to some art classes.
Do you fancy going to art classes at the youth club with me?
OK. I haven’t done much art before, but that won’t matter.
Of course not!
Do you think we’ll do still life pictures, where you draw an object in front of you – fruit or whatever? That’d probably be better for me.
Well, here’s the website, let’s see … It says classes will cover a variety of topics and include painting, both indoors and outside.
I wonder what that will involve? I’ll have to go and find out. Though I’d prefer pencil drawing to painting.
Nine. You will hear two students talking about the school canteen.
I’m glad we’ve got a canteen – I’ve heard lots of schools don’t have them, so we’re quite lucky and the food’s not too expensive either.
Right, so everyone can afford to buy lunch. They seem to have the same meals a lot, though – like, a pasta dish two days in a row.
Well, you can usually find something different to have every day. It’s just that the queues are so long.
Tell me about it – it’d be great if there wasn’t so much standing around waiting for our meals. At least they’re usually tasty!
I know.
Ten. You will hear two friends talking about a TV talent show.
I heard you’re thinking of entering that TV talent show.
Yeah. It’s a great opportunity … and it’ll be fun!
I think you’d be crazy even to think about it. I mean, you
are
talented, but those shows just aim to make the people performing on them look silly.
You’ve always said I could be a professional singer. I might even come first.
It’s a bit more complicated than that. There’ll be loads of serious people competing.
Yeah you probably could, but is that how you want to start your career?
Mmm – I hadn’t really thought about it that seriously.
Eleven. You will hear two friends talking about a homework project.
How are you getting on with your homework project?
OK I think. Although I’m spending far too long online looking things up.
Oh – is it hard to get what you need?

The opposite – it’s more that there’s so much out there! And everything I discover makes me want to know more. Robot technology wasn’t something I was familiar with really. I don’t know why not – it’s an important subject, and something I think most people have an opinion on.
Well, you will too by the time you’ve finished!
I certainly will!
Twelve. You will hear two friends talking about sport on TV.
Do you watch much sport on TV?

Well, I’d like to watch more, but there always seems to be so much football and rugby on. It’d be good if there were other things on too. I don’t mind the conversations they have about matches with all the experts sitting around chatting. That can be quite interesting actually.
So, what would you rather see?

Gymnastics, or basketball, or even hockey – that’s hardly ever shown. I could watch some of the gymnastics stuff again and again. You always notice something different each time. Although some people would probably find that boring!
Thirteen. You will hear a girl talking to a friend about collecting wild food in the woods.
I went on this wild food walk at the weekend, in the woods.
What do you mean?

Well, you’ll probably think it’s boring, but it was about identifying different types of herbs and fruits growing wild. We were hunting for things to eat. It’s what people did hundreds of years ago. It’s food that’s free, fresh and tasty!
Oh, right. What did you find?
Wild garlic leaves, and plants called elderflowers – they’re used to make cold drinks. I might go on another walk in the autumn to identify what mushrooms are safe to eat.
Well, it’s not my kind of thing.
That is the end of Part Two.
Now look at Part Three.
For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one or two words or a number or a date or a time. Look at questions 14 to 19 now. You have 20 seconds.
You will hear a teacher giving information about a school trip to a history museum.

Listen carefully please everyone, I’ve got some information about our trip to the City History Museum tomorrow. We’re going there by coach. It’ll leave at half past eight, but we’d like everybody to be at school ready to board by eight fifteen at the latest, and our coach should arrive as the museum opens at nine o’clock.

It’s not too far away. You’ll need some water, but no other drinks for the journey. You’ll be provided with a packed lunch when we get there, but can I remind you that you are not allowed to eat on the coach.

When we arrive, you’ll get a questionnaire to do as you go round the exhibitions, which I’ll collect from you to check afterwards. The museum will give you a pen too, which you can use, and it’ll be a nice souvenir of the day.

The museum has lots of interesting displays to see. My favourite one is of an old-fashioned street, where you can experience the sights, smells and sounds of life 150 years ago – you may even see someone making bread to a traditional recipe. I know you’ll love the latest display about how chocolate was made in a city in the past – everyone who goes to the museum talks about it!
The museum does have a shop and at the end of the day, you can look round it. They have lots of excellent books and a great range of posters. A variety of food can be bought at a snack shop nearby.
If you or your parents would like to find out more about the museum before we visit, you can look at the website: www dot W-A-Y-S-B-U-R-Y dot com. Did you get that? Any questions?
That is the end of Part Three.
Now look at Part Four. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Look at questions 20 to 25 now. You have 45 seconds.
You will hear an interview with a teenager called Mary Lyons, who started a skateboarding club for girls.
Today I’m talking to 15-year-old Mary Lyons, who set up a skateboarding club for girls in her area. So Mary, how did your interest in skateboarding actually begin?

Well, there was an after school skateboarding session for students in classes above me and I used to pass it on my way home. I liked the look of it so I tried to persuade my brothers to get skateboards so we could learn together, but it wasn’t their thing. And later I learnt more from a programme about skateboarding on TV, and soon I was skateboarding every weekend.
Then, you started a skateboarding club for girls. Why?

Well, people thought it was because I didn’t like being the only girl at the skate park, but in fact, I didn’t mind that. Once I had started, though, I felt it’d be a great idea to encourage other girls to get involved as well. And of course, we still enjoy skateboarding with boys sometimes.
And did everyone support you?

My parents did. But some people were a bit annoying. Saying things like, ‘Why don’t you take up something less dangerous, a sport like tennis.’ I don’t think they realised how few accidents there are, especially if you’re fit and you practise a lot. But at least the town council agreed to support the club financially, which I didn’t really expect.
Has anything surprised you?

Well, I guess I’m amazed that all the club members like each other so much. You know, outside skateboarding, they’d probably never meet. There are members at all levels – which is what you’d probably expect. And I’ve found that people respect me, but well, I started the club so actually I can understand that.
And the champion skateboarder Judy Blake visited the club, didn’t she?

Yes, she did. For us, she’s such a huge star, that, you know, some of us were a bit embarrassed to skate in front of her at first. But that feeling soon went. And she started suggesting loads of things we could do to improve our performances, as well as websites with great videos and stuff like that.
Cool. So, any plans for the future, Mary?

Well, now skateboarding’s been accepted as an Olympic sport, my greatest ambition is to take part. I don’t mind admitting that. It’ll attract more attention from big companies that produce equipment too. When skateboarders get older, some train to become skateboarding instructors. But that’s not what I’m thinking about at the moment.
Thank you, Mary. And good luck with your future.
That is the end of Part Four.
You now have six minutes to write your answers on the answer sheet.
You have one more minute.
That is the end of the test.
